theory.intro: To **solve an absolute value equation** $|ax + b| = k$, split it into two cases: $ax + b = k$ or $ax + b = -k$. Solve each linear equation and check for extraneous solutions.
facts: For $k > 0$, $|ax + b| = k$ splits into two linear equations: $ax + b = k$ and $ax + b = -k$.
For $k = 0$, the equation $|ax + b| = 0$ has one solution given by $ax + b = 0$.
If $k < 0$, the equation $|ax + b| = k$ has **no solution** because an absolute value is never negative.
In $|ax + b| = cx + d$, any candidate solution that makes $cx + d < 0$ is an **extraneous solution** and is rejected.
An equation $|ax + b| = |cx + d|$ splits into $ax + b = cx + d$ or $ax + b = -(cx + d)$.
Substitute all candidate solutions back into the original equation to verify validity.
steps: Check if the constant right-hand side is negative; if so, state no solution
Split the equation into Case 1 ($ax + b = k$) and Case 2 ($ax + b = -k$)
Check each candidate root in the original equation and reject any extraneous solutions

foundation.solution_text:
$\text{Case 1: } x - 4 = 7 \implies x = 11$
$\text{Case 2: } x - 4 = -7 \implies x = -3$
$\text{Check } x = 11: |11 - 4| = |7| = 7 \text{ (valid)}$
$\text{Check } x = -3: |-3 - 4| = |-7| = 7 \text{ (valid)}$
$x = 11 \text{ or } x = -3$

$\text{Case 1: } 2x + 5 = 9 \implies 2x = 4 \implies x = 2$
$\text{Case 2: } 2x + 5 = -9 \implies 2x = -14 \implies x = -7$
$\text{Check } x = 2: |2(2) + 5| = |9| = 9 \text{ (valid)}$
$\text{Check } x = -7: |2(-7) + 5| = |-9| = 9 \text{ (valid)}$
$x = 2 \text{ or } x = -7$

$\text{Case 1: } 3x - 6 = 12 \implies 3x = 18 \implies x = 6$
$\text{Case 2: } 3x - 6 = -12 \implies 3x = -6 \implies x = -2$
$\text{Check } x = 6: |3(6) - 6| = |12| = 12 \text{ (valid)}$
$\text{Check } x = -2: |3(-2) - 6| = |-12| = 12 \text{ (valid)}$
$x = 6 \text{ or } x = -2$

$\text{The absolute value of any real expression is non-negative: } |x + 8| \ge 0.$
$\text{Since the right-hand side is negative } (-4 < 0), \text{ there are no real values of } x \text{ that satisfy the equation.}$
$\text{No solution}$

$\text{Since } |4x - 1| \ge 0 \text{ for all real } x, \text{ it cannot equal the negative constant } -5.$
$\text{No solution}$

|x - 3| = 8
$\text{Case 1: } x - 3 = 8 \implies x = 11$
$\text{Case 2: } x - 3 = -8 \implies x = -5$
$\text{Check } x = 11: \left|\frac{11 - 3}{4}\right| = \left|\frac{8}{4}\right| = 2 \text{ (valid)}$
$\text{Check } x = -5: \left|\frac{-5 - 3}{4}\right| = \left|\frac{-8}{4}\right| = 2 \text{ (valid)}$
$x = 11 \text{ or } x = -5$

development.solution_text:
$\text{Case 1: } 5 - 2x = 7 \implies -2x = 2 \implies x = -1$
$\text{Case 2: } 5 - 2x = -7 \implies -2x = -12 \implies x = 6$
$\text{Check } x = -1: |5 - 2(-1)| = |7| = 7 \text{ (valid)}$
$\text{Check } x = 6: |5 - 2(6)| = |-7| = 7 \text{ (valid)}$
$x = -1 \text{ or } x = 6$

|2x + 7| = 15
$\text{Case 1: } 2x + 7 = 15 \implies 2x = 8 \implies x = 4$
$\text{Case 2: } 2x + 7 = -15 \implies 2x = -22 \implies x = -11$
$\text{Check } x = 4: \left|\frac{2(4) + 7}{3}\right| = \left|\frac{15}{3}\right| = 5 \text{ (valid)}$
$\text{Check } x = -11: \left|\frac{2(-11) + 7}{3}\right| = \left|\frac{-15}{3}\right| = 5 \text{ (valid)}$
$x = 4 \text{ or } x = -11$

$\text{Case 1: } 2x + 1 = 3x \implies x = 1$
$\text{Case 2: } 2x + 1 = -3x \implies 5x = -1 \implies x = -\frac{1}{5}$
$\text{Check } x = 1: |2(1) + 1| = 3 \text{ and } 3(1) = 3 \implies 3 = 3 \text{ (valid)}$
$\text{Check } x = -\frac{1}{5}: \left|2\left(-\frac{1}{5}\right) + 1\right| = \frac{3}{5} \text{ but } 3\left(-\frac{1}{5}\right) = -\frac{3}{5} \implies \frac{3}{5} \ne -\frac{3}{5} \text{ (extraneous)}$
$x = 1$

$\text{Case 1: } x - 3 = 2x \implies x = -3$
$\text{Case 2: } x - 3 = -2x \implies 3x = 3 \implies x = 1$
$\text{Check } x = -3: |-3 - 3| = 6 \text{ but } 2(-3) = -6 \implies 6 \ne -6 \text{ (extraneous)}$
$\text{Check } x = 1: |1 - 3| = 2 \text{ and } 2(1) = 2 \implies 2 = 2 \text{ (valid)}$
$x = 1$

$\text{Case 1: } x - 5 = 2x - 6 \implies -x = -1 \implies x = 1$
$\text{Case 2: } x - 5 = -(2x - 6) \implies x - 5 = -2x + 6 \implies 3x = 11 \implies x = \frac{11}{3}$
$\text{Check } x = 1: |1 - 5| = 4 \text{ but } 2(1) - 6 = -4 \implies 4 \ne -4 \text{ (extraneous)}$
$\text{Check } x = \frac{11}{3}: \left|\frac{11}{3} - 5\right| = \frac{4}{3} \text{ and } 2\left(\frac{11}{3}\right) - 6 = \frac{4}{3} \text{ (valid)}$
$x = \frac{11}{3}$

$\text{Case 1: } 2x - 3 = x + 6 \implies x = 9$
$\text{Case 2: } 2x - 3 = -(x + 6) \implies 2x - 3 = -x - 6 \implies 3x = -3 \implies x = -1$
$\text{Check } x = 9: |2(9) - 3| = 15 \text{ and } |9 + 6| = 15 \text{ (valid)}$
$\text{Check } x = -1: |2(-1) - 3| = 5 \text{ and } |-1 + 6| = 5 \text{ (valid)}$
$x = 9 \text{ or } x = -1$

$\text{Case 1: } 2x + 4 = x - 5 \implies x = -9$
$\text{Case 2: } 2x + 4 = -(x - 5) \implies 2x + 4 = -x + 5 \implies 3x = 1 \implies x = \frac{1}{3}$
$\text{Check } x = -9: |2(-9) + 4| = 14 \text{ but } -9 - 5 = -14 \implies 14 \ne -14 \text{ (extraneous)}$
$\text{Check } x = \frac{1}{3}: \left|2\left(\frac{1}{3}\right) + 4\right| = \frac{14}{3} \text{ but } \frac{1}{3} - 5 = -\frac{14}{3} \implies \frac{14}{3} \ne -\frac{14}{3} \text{ (extraneous)}$
$\text{No solution}$

mastery.solution_text:
$\text{Case 1: } 1 - 3x = 2x + 4 \implies -5x = 3 \implies x = -\frac{3}{5}$
$\text{Case 2: } 1 - 3x = -(2x + 4) \implies 1 - 3x = -2x - 4 \implies -x = -5 \implies x = 5$
$\text{Check } x = -\frac{3}{5}: \left|1 - 3\left(-\frac{3}{5}\right)\right| = \frac{14}{5} \text{ and } 2\left(-\frac{3}{5}\right) + 4 = \frac{14}{5} \text{ (valid)}$
$\text{Check } x = 5: |1 - 3(5)| = |-14| = 14 \text{ and } 2(5) + 4 = 14 \text{ (valid)}$
$x = -\frac{3}{5} \text{ or } x = 5$

$\text{Case 1: } 3x + 1 = 2x - 9 \implies x = -10$
$\text{Case 2: } 3x + 1 = -(2x - 9) \implies 3x + 1 = -2x + 9 \implies 5x = 8 \implies x = \frac{8}{5}$
$\text{Check } x = -10: |3(-10) + 1| = 29 \text{ and } |2(-10) - 9| = 29 \text{ (valid)}$
$\text{Check } x = \frac{8}{5}: \left|3\left(\frac{8}{5}\right) + 1\right| = \frac{29}{5} \text{ and } \left|2\left(\frac{8}{5}\right) - 9\right| = \frac{29}{5} \text{ (valid)}$
$x = -10 \text{ or } x = \frac{8}{5}$

$\text{Case 1: } 4x - 7 = 3x - 1 \implies x = 6$
$\text{Case 2: } 4x - 7 = -(3x - 1) \implies 4x - 7 = -3x + 1 \implies 7x = 8 \implies x = \frac{8}{7}$
$\text{Check } x = 6: |4(6) - 7| = 17 \text{ and } 3(6) - 1 = 17 \text{ (valid)}$
$\text{Check } x = \frac{8}{7}: \left|4\left(\frac{8}{7}\right) - 7\right| = \frac{17}{7} \text{ and } 3\left(\frac{8}{7}\right) - 1 = \frac{17}{7} \text{ (valid)}$
$x = 6 \text{ or } x = \frac{8}{7}$
